TWO MALE CHINESE ARRESTED AT ROOM 628 NANKING
HOTEL, AT REQUEST OF JAPANESE MILITARY POLICE
SUSPECTED TO BE CONCERNED IN BOMB THROWING.

At about 3p.m., Tuesday, Feb. 1, 1938, a message was
received from the Japanese Military Police Office,
Jessfield Road reporting that they desired to release the
prisoner Tsz Keu Ching (〔此处转录不清〕), age 22 years, M/unemployed
teacher, N.P.A. who was arrested in the type setting office
of the Sin Wan Pao No. 274 Hankow Road on Sunday, January
16, 1938.

This prisoner was brought to Central Station by
D. S. Kobayashi at about 4.20p.m. Feb. 1, from the above
Military Office.

According to the report made by the Japanese Military
Authorities this prisoner while being interrogated attempt-
ed to break away and was found to have loosened his cord
handcuffs which resulted in him being struck by one of the
guards on the head causing a small superficial wound of
the scalp.

The prisoner was questioned by D.S.I. Tilton, D.S.
Kobayashi and C.D.S. 111 at Central Station and admitted
that the Japanese Military officers were questioning him
and believed that he was about to escape as he was holding
his head down and did not respond to the Japanese officers
who spoke to him at the time. The prisoner stated this
occurred on Jan. 16, following his arrest and

两名中国男子在南京饭店628室被捕，系应日本宪兵队要求，涉嫌参与投掷炸弹案。

1938年2月1日，星期二，下午3时许，收到来自极司菲尔路日本宪兵队办公室的消息，称他们希望释放囚犯 Tsz Keu Ching（〔此处转录不清〕），22岁，男性/无业教师，北平公安局（N.P.A.）人员，该人于1938年1月16日星期日在汉口路274号《新闻报》排字房被捕。

该囚犯由小林警佐（D. S. Kobayashi）于2月1日下午4时20分左右从上述宪兵队办公室带至中央捕房。

根据日本军方当局的报告，该囚犯在接受审讯时试图逃脱，被发现松开了绳制手铐，导致一名警卫击打其头部，造成头皮轻微浅表伤口。

该囚犯在中央捕房接受蒂尔顿侦探副督察（D.S.I. Tilton）、小林警佐（D. S. Kobayashi）和第111号华人侦探长（C.D.S. 111）的讯问，并承认日本军官当时正在审问他，且认为他企图逃跑，因为他低着头，没有回应当时对他讲话的日本军官。该囚犯称此事发生在1月16日他被捕后，以及

Central 17/1/38 Clerk Fen.

My name is Li Yoh Jing, age 33 years, native of Ningpo, residing at No. 147 Rue Palikao French Concession. I am now unemployed and was formerly a boiler attendant or fireman.

I joined the plain clothes Chinese troops 2nd Regiment in Nantao in June 1937 and my captain was Tseu Chi Dong (周法棠). I left Nantao at the time of the retreat of the Chinese troops during Nov. 1937 and took refuge in the French Concession at No. 147 Rue Palikao. I left for Ningpo later and then returned to Shanghai to find employment, where I met my friend Zau Ah Kung (赵阿公) again. Zau was formerly a captain in the plain clothes troops 1st Regiment in Nantao. Zau asked me to join guerrilla group operating in Shanghai to throw hand grenades. I refused to join and returned to Ningpo during December. I returned to Shanghai again on Jan. 5, 1938 to seek employment and met Zau again at No. 11 Zung Kyih Li (仁吉里) Rue Forte de l'Ouest. I intended to borrow money from him but he refused. I last met Tseu Chi Dong on Jan. 7 or 8, 1938 at the Chah Loh Hotel (爵禄) Room 86 Yu Ya Ching Road. I do not know whether Tseu Chi Dong is a member of the organization with Zau in throwing hand grenades.

My name is Yang Vung Ping alias Yang Kwang Lai (杨光礼即

residing at No. 11 Zung Kyih Li (众志里) Rue Porte de L'Ouest,
French Concession where I was arrested on Jan. 16, 1937.
    I was escorted to the Loh Kah Wei Police Station of the
French Police at about 4p.m., Jan. 17 where I was confronted
with 11 male Chinese arraigned in an identification parade.
I picked out a male Chinese who I recognised as a friend of one
named Tseu Chi Dong (周志东). Tseu is already in custody of the
Japanese Military Authorities and he was a Chief guerrilla who
operated in Shanghai bombing Japanese traitors or other persons
or places according to instructions. I am also a member of the
same group. The man I picked out in the identification parade
previously visited No. 11 Zung Kyih Li, Rue Porte de L'ouest to
call on Tseu Chi Dong my chief, but I cannot say whether this
man is a member of the group. I last saw this man about four
or five days ago at the above address when he called with Tseu
Chi Dong to meet another chief of a similar group named Zau Ah
Kung (赵阿公) who I understand has not been arrested. Zau Ah
Kung holds the same rank as Tseu Chi Dong.
    I have been connected with the throwing of four bombs while
engaged in this work and my statement is the truth.

我叫杨云平，又名杨光礼（即杨之广），21岁，云南人，印刷工，此前居住在法租界西门路（Rue Porte de L'Ouest）众志里（Zung Kyih Li）11号，我于1937年1月16日在此被捕。

Voluntary statement of accused named Tseu Chi Dong (周继东),
alias Yu Jen Zai (于仁才), aged 34, native of Ningpo, residing at
No.143 Rue Palikao, French Concession, taken at the Western
Branch of the Japanese Gendarmerie on January 14, 1938.

"I have been engaged in anti-Japanese activities ever since
the outbreak of the Sino-Japanese conflict and on or about Sept.
10, 1937 I joined the 2nd company of the 7th battalion of the
Flying Column in Shanghai. I am a company commander and I have
21 men under me. I joined this group for the sake of earning my
living. About three years ago I became acquainted with a Chinese
mechanic named Lao Ah Kung (老阿公) when I went to repair printing
machines at the Chung Hwa Printing Co. (中华书局), where Lau was
employed. It was Lao who introduced me to join the Flying Column.

With regard to the organization of the Flying Column, I am
not very familiar with same for Lao Ah Kung keeps all the documents
relating to this matter, but I can tell you what little I know
about it. The Commander-in-Chief is Tu Yuan Hung (杜元洪) and
among the detachment leaders are Chu Hsueh Han (朱学范), committee
member of the Shanghai General Labour Union, and Loh Ching Sz
(陆京士), Chief of Military Court of the Woosung & Shanghai
Garrison Headquarters. Loh had many members under him whose names
I am unable to recall. His men fled to Hongkong and Hankow follow-
ing the retreat of Chinese troops from Shanghai. I know two
leading members of the Flying Column in Shanghai at present. They
are S Zung Yuen (施仲元), about 36 years of age, who is the Chief
of the 7th battalion and another man named Dzung Lih Rong (张立荣),
aged about 34 years. I still hold the post of commander of the
2nd company (or 2nd division) but there is no written certificate
of any kind for the commission. I enlisted with the Flying Column
on or about 14-9-37 on the recommendation of Lao Ah Kung, with pay
at $36 per month. Originally I had 21 men under me but at present
there is 11 men left, the others having absconded in the meantime.
The object of the Flying Column is to harrass the rear of the
Japanese forces by means of guerrilla warfare. Each member of my
company receives $10 a month and the funds were received thr**〔此处转录不清〕**

被告周继东（Tseu Chi Dong），别名于仁才（Yu Jen Zai），34岁，宁波人，住法租界霞飞路（Rue Palikao）143号，于1938年1月14日在日本宪兵队西部分队所作的自愿供述。

“自中日冲突爆发以来，我一直从事反日活动，大约在1937年9月10日左右，我加入了上海别动队第七大队第二中队。我是中队长，手下有21人。我加入这个团体是为了谋生。大约三年前，我去中华书局（Chung Hwa Printing Co.）修理印刷机时，结识了一位在那里受雇的中国技工，名叫老阿公（Lao Ah Kung）。是老阿公介绍我加入别动队的。

关于别动队的组织结构，我不太熟悉，因为所有相关文件都由老阿公保管，但我可以告诉你们我所知道的一点情况。总指挥是杜元洪（Tu Yuan Hung），分队领导人包括上海市总工会委员朱学范（Chu Hsueh Han），以及吴淞上海警备司令部军法处处长陆京士（Loh Ching Sz）。陆手下有许多成员，他们的名字我已记不起来。在中国军队从上海撤退后，他的人逃往了香港和汉口。目前我知道在上海的别动队两名主要成员。他们是施仲元（S Zung Yuen），约36岁，任第七大队大队长；另一人名叫张立荣（Dzung Lih Rong），约34岁。我仍担任第二中队（或第二分队）队长职务，但没有任何书面委任状。我于1937年9月14日左右经老阿公推荐加入别动队，月薪36元。起初我手下有21人，但目前只剩下11人，其他人在此期间已潜逃。别动队的目的是通过游击战骚扰日军后方。我公司每名成员每月领取10元，资金是通过**〔此处转录不清〕**收到的

Dzung Lih Kong and Zao Ah Kung. Our offices are kept a strict
secret. They are located at:
(1) No. unknown, Se Meng Li (西門里), Rue Porte de l'Ouest,
(西門), French Concession.
(2) No. 69 Van Ah Fong (范阿芳), Avenue Dubail.
Dzung Lih Kong lives in Avenue Dubail address. Messages are
sent through orderlies or given out at a daily meeting.
The following is the gist of work done by me in connection
with anti-Japanese activities:
On 26-12-37 at about 3 p.m. five handgrenades and at 3 p.m.
on 29-12-37 four handgrenades and five incendiary bombs (made of
bottle measuring about 8 inches high and wrapped in newspaper)
were received from Dzung from the French Concession. We were told
that instructions will be given later as to how they should be
handled. These infernal machines were delivered to us by a member
of the Flying Column disguised as a messenger of the telegraph
office who had them concealed in a suitcase. They were taken
delivery at No.....(unknown) Pah Ker Li (白克里), Park Road, the
residence of my cousin named Wong Moh Chang (黃木長).
N.B. This house was raided with the assistance of the Sinza
Police Station on 1-1-38, but Wong had already absconded when the
Police visited the house and none of the infernal machines
mentioned above could be recovered.
The nine handgrenades and five incendiary bombs were hidden
in a small room in Wong's house and I also left my automatic pistol,
which I received from my superior officer, at his house.
With regard to our activities in the Settlement I have to
state that on 1-1-38 I was given instructions by company commander
Dzung Lih Kong to throw bombs at the Office of Nisshin Kisen Kaisha
in Canton Road, The Nippon Menka Kaisha in Hankow Road and Toyo
Murakami & Co. in Kiangse Road. Three men under my command named
Fong Sing Hwa (方星華), Hung Yuen Tuh (洪元度) and Yao Ching Dah
(姚景達) were to undertake the work. Fong and Hung were each handed
a handgrenade out of the nine we had by the company commander at
room 26, Sing Tseu (星租) Lodging House, Canton Road, at about 9 a.m.
on 1-1-38.

以下是我在反活动方面所做工作的要点：
1937年12月26日下午3点左右收到五枚手榴弹，1937年12月29日下午3点从法租界的张处收到四枚手榴弹和五枚燃烧弹（由约8英寸高的瓶子制成，并用报纸包裹）。我们被告知稍后会给出如何处理这些指令。这些危险装置由一名伪装成电报局信使的别动队成员交付给我们，他将它们藏在一个手提箱里。交货地点是公园路（Park Road）白克里（Pah Ker Li）____号（不详），这是我表弟黄木长（Wong Moh Chang）的住所。

这九枚手榴弹和五枚燃烧弹藏在黄家的一间小房间里，我还把我从上级军官那里得到的自动手枪也留在他家里。
关于我们在租界内的活动，我必须说明，1938年1月1日，我接到中队长张立荣的指示，向广东路的日清汽船株式会社（Nisshin Kisen Kaisha）办事处、汉口路的日本棉花株式会社（The Nippon Menka Kaisha）以及江西路的东洋村上商会（Toyo Murakami & Co.）投掷炸弹。我手下的三名队员，方星华（Fong Sing Hwa）、洪元度（Hung Yuen Tuh）和姚景达（Yao Ching Dah），将执行这项任务。1938年1月1日上午9点左右，在广东路星租旅馆（Sing Tseu Lodging House）26号房间，中队长从我们拥有的九枚手榴弹中分别发给方和洪各一枚。

They were to have thrown them at the first two mentioned addresses
I warned these men to be very careful in handling the bombs and
that they should throw them at 11 a.m. the same day. Fong and
Hung left the lodging house with Yao acting as the supervisor at
9.30 a.m. and proceeded to the scene, but they were unable to
accomplish their task owing to the strong police cordon thrown
immediately after the bomb incident at the corner of Hankow and
Fokien roads. They returned to the lodging house at about 11.30
a.m. carrying with them the two bombs in question. The bombs I
understand were later thrown into a creek.

Three men under my command belonging to Lao Ah
Kung's party assembled at the Ling Tseu lodging house in Canton
Road and each man was given a bomb and a piece of paper bearing
the address to be thrown at. I do not know where Lao's men were
to throw their bombs. I saw Lao's men leave the lodging house,
but I am unable to give you the destination of his men as our
movements are kept secret from one another. I am inclined to
believe, however, that the Flying Column members were also
responsible for the bomb incident which took place more or less
simultaneously the same day at three other places namely, in
Hankow Road, No.3 Hung Dah Cotton Mill and Kiwa No.3 Mill.

Before we set out on 1-1-38 on our mission, we were given
$5.50 for 11 men, i.e. 50 cents for each man. After the above
incidents I went into hiding and divided my time between my house
and Sung Tai Lodging House (生泰栈) at Pah Li Jao. I have been
on the move all the time in order to escape arrest. I left for
Ningpo at 3 p.m. 3-1-38 on "Mei Foo(?)", a German steamer and
returned to Shanghai on 12-1-38, I recognize the pamphlet shown
to me(distributed near the scene of incident on Hankow Road) as
same as those that I saw at the residence of Dzung Lih Mong some
time ago.

属于老阿公派系的三名手下在广东路的灵租旅馆（Ling Tseu lodging house）集合，每人发给一枚炸弹和一张写有投掷地址的纸条。我不知道老的人要把炸弹扔到哪里。我看到老的人离开旅馆，但我无法告诉你他们的人的去向，因为我们的行动彼此保密。不过，我倾向于认为，同一天在其他三个地方几乎同时发生的炸弹事件，即汉口路、鸿达第三棉纺厂（Hung Dah Cotton Mill No.3）和基瓦第三厂（Kiwa No.3 Mill），也是别动队成员所为。

1938年1月1日出发执行任务前，我们11人共获得了5.50美元，即每人50美分。上述事件发生后，我躲藏起来，时间分配在我自己的家和八里桥的生泰栈（Sung Tai Lodging House）之间。为了逃避逮捕，我一直在四处移动。1938年1月3日下午3点，我乘坐德国轮船“美孚号”（Mei Foo(?)）前往宁波，并于1938年1月12日返回上海。我认出向我展示的小册子（在汉口路事件现场附近分发）与我前段时间在张立蒙（Dzung Lih Mong）住所看到的一样。

At 8 a.m. Friday, January 14th 1938, Sergeant Major
Kobata of the Japanese Military Police together with four
other Japanese officials attended Central Station and
requested assistance to make a raid on Room No.628 Nanking
Hotel, Shanse Road, to arrest certain Chinese implicated
by other male Chinese in custody by the Japanese authorit-
ies as being concerned in throwing bombs in the
International Settlement on January 1st 1938(place not
divulged). The Senior Detective i/c informed the D.O. "A"
who instructed that the assistance be rendered.

D.S.I. Tilton with D.S. Kobayashi together with the
Japanese officials as mentioned, and party of Chinese
detectives attached to Central Station carried out the
raid at 8.14 a.m. above date. Two male Chinese were found
sleeping in the room together with four Chinese females.
The latter were allowed to go being girl guides while the
two men were taken into custody and escorted to Central
Station.

The room was searched which failed to disclose any
arms, weapons or missiles, and no incriminating evidence
was found in the room to indicate that these men had
connections with any criminal gang. A quantity of printed

official of the Shanghai Woosung Garrison.

The motor car was accordingly seized by the
Japanese Authorities, who licenced it (S.M.C. Licence

因此，该汽车被日本当局扣押，他们为其颁发了执照（公共租界执照号码5509），并将其用作诱饵，旨在定位并确认车主身份，推测车主为陆京士或任何可能曾与他有过关联的人——以便对他们进行讯问。还暗示，如果

Mr. Yuling L. Wu and Yang, Pei Jan not staying at this
Station until 9.30 a.m. on the 10.2.38, and in the event

the Shanghai Municipal Police would be held more or less

Taking into consideration the foregoing, Mr.
Robertson, Divisional Officer in charge of "A" Division
was communicated with and the subject of this report
outlined to him, who in turn communicated with Mr. Alers,

made fully conversant with that which the Japanese
Authorities desired, also the facts and reasons leading
to their request. This they voluntarily acceded to making

Further, regarding the motor car it was pointed out,
the Police desired that it be left at this Station, but
should the Japanese Authorities insist that it be returned
to them, this would be complied with, with a proviso
that they would assume full responsibility for the vehicle.
However, the Authorities insisted that the vehicle be
returned to them; this was accordingly done, the car
being handed over to Mr. Nakanishi, agent of the Japanese
Gendarmerie Intelligence Department, who signed the
Detained Property Book.

考虑到上述情况，已与负责“A”分区的分区警官罗伯逊（Robertson）先生取得联系，并向他概述了本报告的主题，他随即与负责各分区的副总监阿勒斯（Alers）先生取得联系，根据阿勒斯先生的指示，吴玉麟先生和杨沛然充分了解了日本当局的愿望，以及导致其请求的事实和原因。他们自愿同意并签署了附后的陈述书。

此外，关于该汽车，指出警方希望将其留在本捕房，但如果日本当局坚持要求归还给他们，将会照办，前提是他们对该车辆承担全部责任。然而，当局坚持要求归还车辆；于是照办了，车辆被移交给日本宪兵队情报部代理人中西（Nakanishi，音译）先生，他在《扣留财产登记簿》上签了字。

Copy of statement of Chow Ying-chiu, taken at Louza
Station on February 9, 1938
------

My name is Chow Ying-chiu, aged 30 years, native of
Kiangsu, residing at No.90 Zai Loh Fang, Rue du Capitaine
Rebier, French Concession. I was formerly employed as a
chauffeur by a doctor named Chao Tse Zeu for one year.
On April, 29th, 1937, the doctor recommended me to his
friend Wu Yu Ling who had bought a second hand "Standard"
motor car.

My present master Wu Yu Ling resided in Lane 640
Seward Road prior to hostilities and when not in use the
car was parked in the alleyway.

Upon the outbreak of hostilities my master Wu Yu Ling
removed to Lane No.271 Avenue Joffre, French Concession,
and the car when not in use was parked in the alleyway.

At the end of the year 1937 my master stopped using
the car and instructed me to find some safe place to keep
the car, there being no known garage in the vicinity.

On January 3rd, 1938 through the introduction of my
friend, a chauffeur named Tsai Siau Hsiang, I removed the
car to the garage of an unoccupied house No.462 Jessfield
Road which was then watched by one named Wong Sing Woo.
In the meantime the licence of the car was returned to the
F.M.C.

On January 24th, 1938, my master Wu Yu Ling accompanied
me to the aforesaid place to examine the car but on arriving
there we found it missing, the caretaker Wong Siau Hsiang
could not be located and both front and back doors of the
premises were locked inside. In the afternoon of same date
my master reported the loss to Bubbling Well Police Station.

In the afternoon of February 9, 1938, I was sent for by
my master to Louza Police Station where I identified a motor

------

本人周荫秋，现年30岁，江苏人，现住法租界雷米埃上尉路（Rue du Capitaine Rebier）载禄坊90号。我曾任赵子修（Chao Tse Zeu）医生的司机一年。1937年4月29日，赵医生将我推荐给他的朋友吴玉麟，后者购买了一辆二手“标准”（Standard）牌汽车。

我的现任主人吴玉麟在战事爆发前住于西华德路640弄，汽车不使用时便停在弄堂里。

战事爆发后，我的主人吴玉麟搬至法租界霞飞路271弄，汽车不使用时仍停在弄堂里。

1937年底，我的主人停止使用汽车，并指示我找个安全的地方存放车辆，因为附近没有已知的车库。

1938年1月3日，经我的朋友、司机蔡少香（Tsai Siau Hsiang）介绍，我将车移至静安寺路462号一处无人居住房屋的车库，当时由一名叫王信伍（Wong Sing Woo）的人看管。其间，汽车牌照已交还法公董局（F.M.C.）。

1938年1月24日，我的主人吴玉麟随我前往上述地点查看汽车，但到达后发现车辆失踪，看守人王小香（Wong Siau Hsiang）不知去向，该处前后门均从内部锁闭。同日下午，我的主人向静安寺捕房报案失窃。

Statement of Yu Yu Ling, age 45, native of Shanghai
taken at Louza Station on 9-2-38

My name is Yu Yu Ling, aged 45, native of Shanghai,
residing at House No.11. Lane No.271 Avenue Joffre, French
Concession. I am the manager of the China Educational
Supply Company, 406 Foochow Road and the following is my
voluntary statement.

On April 23, 1937, I bought from the Reliance Motor
Company a second hand "Standard" 4 door sedan motor car,
for $1,140.00. The payment was made by instalments, i.e.
I first advanced $640.00 and settled the remaining $500.00
in five months, paying each month $100.00 plus 34 interest.

On April 29, 1937, I obtained a licence No.6588 from
the S.M.C. Later on November 1, having removed to the French
Concession, I obtained a licence No.7〔此处转录不清〕 from the C.M.T.
At the end of the year 1937, owing to business depression
I did not use the car and on January 2, 1938, I returned the
licence to the C.M.T., meanwhile I instructed my chauffeur
Chow Ying Chiu to keep the vehicle in some safe place which
I later learned was situated at No.442 Jessfield Road. Being
under the impression that this address was located within
a peaceful area, I felt satisfied.

I did not go to the place where the car was kept until
the morning of January 24, when I discovered that it was
missing. At 4.45 p.m. same date I reported the theft at
Bubbling Well Police Station and enquiries were made at the
scene by both foreign and Chinese detectives.

At 9 p.m. on February 9, 1938, a shop apprentice named
Ling Hung Foh of my company told me that the lost car had
been recovered and that it was in custody of Louza Police
Station. I then immediately went to that Police Station
for the car.

本人吴玉麟，现年45岁，上海人，现住法租界霞飞路271弄11号。我是福州路406号中国教育用品公司经理，以下为我的自愿供词。

1937年4月23日，我从信义汽车公司（Reliance Motor Company）以1,140.00美元的价格购买了一辆二手“标准”牌四门轿车。款项分期支付，即我先预付640.00美元，剩余500.00美元在五个月内付清，每月支付100.00美元加34利息。

1937年4月29日，我从工部局获得第6588号牌照。后来于11月1日，因搬至法租界，我从法公董局（C.M.T.）获得第7〔此处转录不清〕号牌照。
1937年底，由于生意萧条，我不再使用该车，并于1938年1月2日将牌照交还法公董局，同时指示我的司机周荫秋将车辆存放在某个安全的地方，后来得知该处位于静安寺路442号。因以为该地址处于和平区域，我感到放心。

直到1月24日上午，我才去存放汽车的地方，发现车辆失踪。同日下午4时45分，我向静安寺捕房报案失窃，中外侦探均在现场进行了调查。

1938年2月9日晚9时，我公司一名叫凌洪发（Ling Hung Foh）的学徒告诉我，丢失的汽车已找回，现由老闸捕房扣押。我随即立即前往该捕房取车。

Statement of Yang Pei Zeu, aged 41, native of Shanghai
taken at Louza Station on 9-2-38

My name is Yang Pei Zeu, aged 41, native of Shanghai,
residing at House No.11 Lane 271 Avenue Joffre, French
Concession. I am a clerk of the S.M.P. and attached to
the 1st S.S.D. Court.

In April 1937, my younger sister's husband named
Tu Yu Ling bought from the Reliance Motor Company a second
hand "Standard" motor car, S.M.C. Licence No.8588 which
was later changed to C.M.T. Licence No.7858.

On the afternoon of January 24, 1938, Tu Yu Ling
told me that his car was missing from Jessfield Road where
he had kept the vehicle. At 4.45 p.m. same date I
accompanied him to Bubbling Well Police Station and
reported the loss.

At about 7 p.m. on February 9, 1938, I received a
telephone message from a shop apprentice named Ling Hung
Foh to the effect that the lost car was found parked on
Foochow Road near Fokien Road. I immediately proceeded
to the said place where I identified the car as the one
reported stolen, because I had used the car several times.
I then telephoned the Louza Police Station and F.S.113
together with two Japanese constables No.9 and 125
respectively attended who brought me and the car to
the station.

I do not know who was the occupier of House No.442
Jessfield Road.

Sd. Yang Pei Zeu.

dated 24/1/38
----------

At 4.45 p.m. 24-1-38 complainant Wu Yu Ling (吴雨霖)
m'manager residing House 11, Lane 271 Avenue Joffre, came
to the station and reported that one unlicenced Standard '4'
m/car, 4 door sedan, black colour, Engine No.186854, value
$1,140.00 had been stolen, from the garage of House 442
Jessfield Road (Chinese number).

Enquiries made by the undersigned, D.S.I. T'ang Tzu
Hung and J.D.S. 176 ascertained that about 2 months ago,
complainant returned the licence plates to the F.M.C., as
he did not desire to use the car during the coming year.

On 7-1-38, he had the car towed to 442 Jessfield Road
where he placed it in the garage. This house was at this
time occupied by Loh Ching Ts (陸京士), formerly employed by the
Shanghai & Woosung Garrison. Later in the month Loh Ching Ts
left, leaving a caretaker named Wong Shing Woo (王信龢) in
charge of the house.

On p.m. 21/1/38, a party of Japanese and Chinese
visited the address, and made enquiries regarding Loh Ching
Ts.

On p.m. 21/1/38, the Chinese returned alone and made
further enquiries.

At 9 a.m. 22/1/38, the above Chinese again returned
and conducted a search of the house and started to remove
some property.

The caretaker become afraid and left the premises.

At 11.30 a.m. 24/1/38, complainant visited the house
and found that new locks had been affixed to the front and
rear doors, and that the garage door had been closed from the
inside. He, however, was able to look through a crack in
the door, and saw that the m/car had been removed.

1938年1月24日下午4时45分，投诉人吴雨霖（Wu Yu Ling），经理，住霞飞路271弄11号，来到巡捕房报案，称一辆无牌照的“标准”牌4型汽车，四门轿车，黑色，发动机号186854，价值1,140.00美元，从极司菲尔路（Jessfield Road）442号（中国门牌号码）的车库内被盗。

经下文签署人、警探长唐子洪（T'ang Tzu Hung）及初级警探176号调查查明，约两个月前，投诉人将车牌交还工部局财务处（F.M.C.），因他不打算在来年使用该车。

1938年1月7日，他让人将车拖至极司菲尔路442号，并存入车库。当时该房屋由陆京士（Loh Ching Ts）居住，他此前受雇于上海吴淞守备区。当月晚些时候，陆京士离开，留一名名叫王信龢（Wong Shing Woo）的看管人负责照看房屋。

1938年1月21日下午，一群日本人和中国人到访该地址，询问有关陆京士的情况。

1938年1月21日下午，那名中国人独自返回，进一步打听情况。

1938年1月22日上午9时，上述中国人再次返回，对房屋进行了搜查，并开始搬走一些财物。

看管人心生恐惧，离开了该处所。

1938年1月24日上午11时30分，投诉人前往该房屋，发现前后门都装上了新锁，车库门也从内部被关上。然而，他透过门缝向内张望，发现汽车已被移走。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
CONFIDENTIAL.
ALLEGED "CACHE" OF HAND GRENADES.

At 9.30 am. 21/1/38, J.L.S. Tanaka, attached to the S.P.O. reported at C.B.H.Q. that he had received an intimation from the chief of the Secret Police of the Japanese Military, that they had received information that a "cache" of grenades were concealed in a certain house within the limits of the Settlement and that they wished the house to be raided by the S.M.P.

The undersigned conferred with L.S. Tanaka and then reported to Supt. MacDermott, who gave permission for the raid to be carried out.

The undersigned then accompanied J.L.S. Tanaka to Room 217 of the Bank of Taiwan Building and there met Captain Mori, Chief of the Secret Gendarmie, who stated that he was in possession of information that 300 or 400, hand grenades had been "cached" in the premises at 442 Jessfield Road.

Captain Mori was informed that Jessfield Road was an outside road and the number mentioned was possibly O.O.L. but to make certain J.L.S. Tanaka and the undersigned would accompany the raiding party to the premises.

At 10.30 a.m. same date, 442 (which is a Chinese number) Jessfield Rd, was entered, but after a thorough search no hand grenades were found.

1938年1月21日上午9时30分，隶属特别警务科（S.P.O.）的日本籍初级警探田中（Tanaka）向中央捕房总部报告称，他收到日本军方秘密警察头目的通知，称他们获悉有一批手榴弹“藏匿”在租界范围内的某所房屋内，希望由工部局警务处对该房屋进行突击搜查。

下文签署人与日本籍初级警探田中商议后，向麦克德莫特（MacDermott）督察长报告，后者批准进行此次突击搜查。

随后，下文签署人陪同日本籍初级警探田中前往台湾银行大楼217室，在那里会见了宪兵队秘密警察队长森（Mori）上尉。森上尉称，他掌握情报，有300或400枚手榴弹“藏匿”在极司菲尔路442号的 premises（房产/处所）内。

已告知森上尉，极司菲尔路属于界外道路，所述门牌号码可能位于越界筑路区域（O.O.L.），但为确保无误，日本籍初级警探田中和下文签署人将随同突击小队前往该处所。

同日（1月21日）上午10时30分，人员进入了极司菲尔路442号（中国门牌号码），但经过彻底搜查，未发现任何手榴弹。
